_comment: claude-dev-practice/README.md promises: 'Every claim points at code in this repo, with the
path. If a document says a thing is enforced, you can go and read the enforcement -- and if you
cannot, that is a bug in the document.' Check A verifies that the citations which EXIST resolve.
It has nothing to say about a section containing none at all, and that is how an entirely
unsourced section shipped: second-longest in the document, zero paths, every check green.
A section registered here is making the weaker claim honestly. Two rules:
- 'reason' is required, and should explain why no path CAN be given, not why one wasn't.
- the document should say so too. A limit recorded only in a registry is a limit the reader
never sees; the point is that they can calibrate how much to trust the section.
Scope is the prose documents that make the promise -- see the scope[] list below, which is
authoritative; do not restate its length here, because appending a document and forgetting the
sentence beside it is exactly how this comment went stale once already. README.md is a map and
VERIFIED-AGAINST.md is a registry with external sources, so neither is held to it.

entries.section: 5. Write it down where it will be read
entries.reason: Names the HOMES knowledge lives in -- the always-on file, a rules file behind a paths glob, a skill, auto-memory. Every one of them is host configuration outside any repository, and the gate excludes host paths by shape precisely because it cannot resolve them. There is no in-repo artefact to point at without inventing one.

entries.section: 6. The tool surface is an input, and it is the one that fails quietly
entries.reason: No MCP server lives in this repository, and naming an internal one would fail the redaction check -- correctly, since these documents are written to be readable outside the organisation. The section states this limit in its own text so a reader can weigh it, rather than leaving it recorded only here.
States the shape every mutating operation should take. It is a pattern, not an implementation; the sections that follow carry the implementations and their paths.

Built entirely from external incidents -- tar over a junction, a secret scanner in a worktree. The commands are quoted so a reader can reproduce them; the failures happened to third-party tools, so there is no file here that embodies them.

entries.section: 4. Know what is actually recoverable before you rely on it
entries.reason: A table of recovery properties per store -- git, a session checkpoint, a graph write, an untracked directory. These are properties of the stores themselves. The checkpoint row is sourced instead through VERIFIED-AGAINST.md, which pins it to a version and a date.
